items.rationale: Dismantling and refitting to place drying equipment is covered under technical drying (5.2.7). Priced at the near-identical reference level of 84-95.
Technical drying (5.2.7) is covered for the documented drying period; 7 days are invoiced, within the roughly two weeks of drying described. Reference and prior give about 45/day, so about 313.

Under 7.4.4 a surcharge is paid only against an itemised list of the materials it relates to; the description calls it unexplained, so it is likely 0. Under 5.2.7 the dryer flat rate also already includes its ancillaries.
A standard mineral-wool shell for the repaired pipe is within the 7.14(c) standard; reference level is about 26.
Under 5.2.1 debris removal is reimbursed once per event and only the first charge counts; this drying invoice (0097) comes first. Reference level is 58-61.
Re-levelling the substrate is part of making good under 5.2.6. Reference level is about 38.
Substrate preparation in the damage area counts as making good (5.2.6). The rate is estimated at about 40/m² over 2.78 m²; it may partly overlap with the levelling line.
Creating the access opening needed to reach the pipe is covered under 5.2.6. Moderate price estimate.
The 90x90 format is within the 7.14(d) threshold, so replacement tiles are covered. 5 pcs is about 4 m², consistent with the area plus cutting waste; priced at an upper customary level.
This format exceeds the 90x90 threshold and is designer grade, so 3.5(a) and 3.5(f) exclude any payment. It also duplicates line 9 (3.5(d)).
Standard sanitary silicone for the reinstated tiling is covered. Reference is about 13/m, so about 47 for 3.6 m.
Under 7.4.2 one travel charge is paid per contractor per document, and this is the only one on the tiling invoice. Reference level is 82-84.
Labour for the covered tiling and making good is reimbursed at customary rates (7.4.1). The reference had 14 hrs at 1260 or more.

items.description: Remove drywall and insulation wool basement
items.rationale: Opening up within the basement damage area is covered under 5.2.6. Reference levels were about 50 for drywall and 46 for insulation, so about 100 combined.
Removing damp plaster in the damage area is covered. The per-unit reference and prior are about 29.
The attic is outside the damage area and the work is unrelated to the leak, so 3.5(b) and 7.1.5 exclude it.
This duplicates the disposal already charged by the drying firm; 5.2.1 and 3.5(d) allow only the first charge.
